memories.content: The user's available days and times vary by week, making it difficult to apply last month's free time directly to the next appointment.
The user once canceled an appointment booked for the same weekday as in the previous month.
When asked again about availability just before booking, the user provided three free times for that week.
On a day with two consecutive morning appointments, the user ate lunch at 3 p.m.
On a day the user left an hour between appointments, they ate while traveling.
After seeing a private reason written directly in a calendar title, the user removed the wording.
The user checked that a calendar-sharing screen showed only the time and hid the details.
When evening plans on the same day must change, the user's mother wants advance notice on the weekend morning.
The local agent cannot know the private reason for unavailability from the unavailable time alone.
The user's shared calendar does not automatically reserve travel time between events.
One of the user's identity documents needs renewal in the second half of 2025.
The user postponed an application until the next day after spending time looking for document photos in scattered folders.
After gathering the necessary copies in one folder, the user completed the renewal form in one sitting.
The user entered an abbreviated name on an official form and then discovered that it differed from the supporting document.
On the next application, after comparing the name with the source document, the user did not receive a correction request.
The user put only the submission deadline in the calendar and missed the application deadline by one day because they did not check the issuance period.
On the next application, the user recorded the expected issuance date separately in the calendar.
Staff at a public-service counter expect a person requesting identity verification to bring an original as well as a copy.
When planning an official application, put both the submission deadline and expected issuance date in the calendar and verify them.
The local agent cannot determine the current validity of an identity document without its expiration date.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational domains without contradiction: one concerns appointment availability, spacing, calendar privacy, and family notice, while the other concerns identity-document renewal, application preparation, form accuracy, required materials, and date tracking. No claims govern the same operational decision closely enough for a cross-frame relation.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories jointly describe variability, a failed reuse of a prior weekday, and successful collection of fresh availability; the compared frame contains no matching availability claim.
relations.summary: Weekly availability varies, so prior scheduling patterns are unreliable and current free times provide the relevant booking information.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories describe consequences of consecutive or narrowly spaced appointments and a calendar limitation that omits travel time; the compared frame does not address appointment buffers.
relations.summary: Appointment spacing and absent travel reservations can leave inadequate time for meals and transit.

relations.reason: Each member concerns preserving the opacity of private calendar information through title removal, restricted sharing, or the inherent limits of an unavailable-time marker; no compared-side claim addresses this privacy policy.
relations.summary: Calendar unavailability can conceal private reasons, and the user removes or hides revealing details.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-side communication expectation with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user’s mother expects weekend-morning advance notice when same-day evening plans must change.

relations.reason: This compared-side renewal fact has no corresponding claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: An identity document requires renewal during the second half of 2025.

relations.reason: The compared-side memories describe contrasting outcomes before and after gathering application materials into one folder; the reference frame does not address file preparation.
relations.summary: Consolidating required document copies avoids search-related delay and supports completing a renewal form in one sitting.

relations.reason: The compared-side memories describe a name mismatch and a later application checked against its source document; no reference-side claim concerns form-name accuracy.
relations.summary: Comparing the entered official name with the supporting document prevents discrepancies and associated correction requests.

relations.reason: The compared-side memories describe the failure caused by tracking only one date, the later separate entry, and the resulting planning rule; the reference frame contains no equivalent application-date policy.
relations.summary: Official applications require separate calendar tracking and verification of both the submission deadline and expected issuance date.

relations.reason: This independently useful compared-side requirement has no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Identity verification at a public-service counter requires bringing both an original document and a copy.

relations.reason: This compared-side information limit concerns document validity, whereas the reference-side agent limitation concerns concealed calendar reasons and does not address the same operational determination.
relations.summary: A local agent cannot determine an identity document’s current validity without its expiration date.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only information covers renewal timing, organizing application files, matching official names, tracking submission and issuance dates, bringing originals and copies, and the limits of assessing validity without an expiration date.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only information covers rechecking weekly availability, allowing practical appointment buffers, protecting calendar privacy, and notifying the user’s mother about same-day evening changes.
